description: One row per person on a deal. The opportunity registry is one row per deal, so it cannot hold a list of people, and a count of them on the deal row cannot tell you which of them actually answers. This is what makes single-threaded a real flag rather than a promise. Contacts are unioned from the CRM's contact-role object AND from who appears in the activity record, because those are different sets — the people formally attached to a deal and the people carrying it are routinely not the same.

columns.name: opportunity_id
columns.note: OPP- id this person is on. The link back to the deal.

columns.name: opportunity_name
columns.note: DERIVED: copied from the deal so the sheet is readable on its own. A file of IDs is a file nobody opens twice.

columns.name: contact_crm_id
columns.note: The person's record in the CRM. Blank for someone who only ever appears in the activity record as an email address.

columns.name: role_crm_id
columns.note: The contact-role record linking this person to this deal. Blank for an activity-only contact — which is itself the signal that they are working the deal without the CRM knowing.

columns.name: email
columns.note: The match key for activity. Where a contact record is missing, this is the only identity there is.

columns.name: role
columns.note: From the org's own contact-role picklist. Left as free text in the shipped schema because no two orgs use the same list; the profile supplies the real values and the Excel dropdown.

columns.name: source
columns.note: DERIVED: where this person came from. `activity-only` means they are talking to you and the CRM does not know they are on the deal. `contact-role` with no activity is the reverse, and is the ghost-roles pattern.

columns.name: outbound_count
columns.note: DERIVED: messages sent to this person. Effort, not interest — it is the denominator that makes no-reply-ever meaningful rather than the signal itself.

columns.name: replied
columns.note: DERIVED and DELIBERATELY NULLABLE. yes / no / blank, where blank means the org's logging cannot support an answer — a CRM whose activity object carries no direction flag genuinely cannot tell an inbound message from an outbound one. Forcing an unknown to `no` manufactures a risk flag out of a logging gap. Read `reply_evidence` before believing either value.

columns.name: reply_evidence
columns.note: DERIVED: how `replied` was decided, strongest first. `direction-flag` is the org's own inbound/outbound field. `sender-inferred` means the record carried a sender address and one side of it was you — a fact about the message, not a guess. `subject-heuristic` is a guess from Re:-style prefixes and matches your own replies too. `no-activity` means there are no messages with this person at all, so `no` is trivially true. `none` means messages exist and direction cannot be established; it is the one value that pairs with a blank `replied`.

columns.name: replies_count
columns.note: DERIVED: genuine replies only. Auto-replies are excluded here and counted in `auto_replies_count`, because an out-of-office proves a mailbox exists and nothing about the person behind it.

columns.name: auto_replies_count
columns.note: DERIVED: inbound messages matching the profile's auto-reply patterns. Kept rather than discarded — a contact whose every inbound is machine-generated needs verifying, and that is a different action from chasing them.

columns.name: meeting_held
columns.note: DERIVED, nullable on the same rule as `replied`. Read with `meeting_evidence`.

columns.name: meeting_evidence
columns.note: DERIVED: which rung of the fallback chain this came from, strongest first. `transcript` is the top rung — the person is on the record speaking in the room, which settles attendance in a way no calendar inference can. Then `opportunity-linked` (frequently near-empty in real orgs, since meetings are rarely linked to deals), `account-dated`, and `invite-accepted` — calendar traffic recovered from email subjects, the weakest. Recorded because a rep deserves to know which they are looking at. contacts_sync folds the meetings registry in on every build, so transcript evidence survives a rebuild.

columns.name: engagement
columns.note: DERIVED. Not a boolean, because these are genuinely different states with different actions: `auto-reply-only` means verify the person before spending more outreach on them, `never-contacted` means the deal has a name attached and nobody has tried. `undetermined` is what an org with no usable direction data gets, and is honest rather than empty.

columns.name: crm_id
columns.note: Match key for sync. The contact-role record where there is one, otherwise a stable synthetic key of opportunity plus email, so an activity-only contact does not get re-inserted on every rebuild.
